name: TimeBridge cross-contract signature-domain collision
summary: TimeToken's mint authorization hash omitted the target contract, so validator-approved payloads from the CGU bridge were also valid mint authorizations on the BNB Chain TIME contract.

loss.notes: Gross victim depletion is the TIME/WBNB pair's two receipt-level WBNB outflows: 49.148868512713910253 + 47.055759351281121339 = 96.204627863995031592 WBNB, with no WBNB input to the pair in either selected sale receipt. The corresponding 50,000 and 469,000 TIME pair inputs equal the preceding mints in full. Those tokens were created from the zero address rather than removed from bridge inventory, so the 519,000 TIME inflation is causal evidence but not an additional loss component. Archive balances reconcile after excluding third-party transactions in the same blocks: 59.066548624489445285 + 0.089715987592328670 - 49.148868512713910253 = 10.007396099367863702 WBNB, and 48.324075110012389377 + 0.147530569832458028 - 47.055759351281121339 = 1.415846328563726066 WBNB. The imported approximately $872,000 figure valued the nominal mint before slippage; it is replaced by exact LP depletion using a separate preceding BNB price for each sale. Later recoveries are not netted.

ageReset.description: TimeToken is a direct, non-proxy contract. Its runtime was absent in the preceding block and is byte-identical at deployment and immediately before both incident mints.

sources.note: Reviewed the eight successful BNB Chain lock, unlock, mint and sale transactions in the two linked sequences; every TIME and WBNB Transfer log in the two sale receipts; every WBNB transfer touching pair 0xa5ebd19961cf4b8af06a9d9d2b91d73b48744867 in both sale blocks; archive WBNB balances; the sender's complete BNB Chain nonce history through nonce 30; the TimeToken deployment and historical runtime; EIP-1967 slots; BscScan's verified TimeToken source; Merkle Science's forensic report; and two independently preceding DefiLlama BNB prices. In the first sequence the sender locks 50,000 CGU at nonce 12, calls CGU unlock at nonce 14, mints 50,000 TIME at nonce 15 and sells the full mint at nonce 16. In the second it locks 469,000 CGU at nonce 19, calls unlock at nonce 22, mints 469,000 TIME at nonce 23 and sells the full mint at nonce 24. For each sequence, the unlock calldata after its selector is byte-identical to the following TimeToken mint calldata, including both validator signatures. Approvals and token acquisition at adjacent nonces have zero TIME/WBNB pair flow; nonce 20 is an unrelated native deposit; nonce 25 onward contains another CGU lock but no later TIME mint or sale. The mint receipts create exactly 5,000,000,000,000 and 46,900,000,000,000 TIME base units, and the following sales transfer those exact amounts into the pair. The pair transfers out exactly 49,148,868,512,713,910,253 and 47,055,759,351,281,121 WBNB wei with no selected-receipt WBNB input. Third-party same-block WBNB inflows of 89,715,987,592,328,670 and 147,530,569,832,458,028 wei explain the difference between receipt outflow and whole-block archive balance change and are excluded from the attacker campaign. The first and second prices precede their respective sales by 101 and 59 seconds. TimeToken was top-level created by the protocol deployer in source-3 at block 8,117,265 index 100, timestamp 1,623,152,974. No code exists at its address in the preceding block; its 16,300-byte runtime hashes to 0xa043d22a5dd47e51b17f2b68d6c17628070f54f7576eadf37c89296883651993 at creation and immediately before both mints. The disassembled runtime contains no DELEGATECALL, CALLCODE or SELFDESTRUCT, and its EIP-1967 implementation, admin and beacon slots are zero. Both incident transactions call mint directly on that unchanged artifact, making deployment the last executable-code event and its age 153,709,803 seconds at the first mint.

notes: The record is scoped to BNB Chain. The CGU bridge activity proves campaign linkage but contributes no measured victim depletion.
